walkthroughs.body_html: Lithosphere (carbonates, fossil fuels) dwarfs others at ~10^8 Gt. Oceans hold ~38000 Gt active carbon. Soils contain ~1500 Gt (more than vegetation 500 Gt). Atmosphere 870 Gt rising ~5 Gt/yr from anthropogenic emissions exceeding sinks.

Surface ocean (top 100 m) holds ~900 Gt and exchanges rapidly with atmosphere. Deep ocean (38000 Gt) cycles over centuries-millennia via thermohaline circulation. Solubility pump (cold water absorbs more CO2) and biological pump (organisms sink to depth) drive transfer.

Forests contain ~360 Gt above ground; soils ~1500 Gt. Tropical peatlands (Indonesia) hold 80 Gt; permafrost ~1500 Gt vulnerable to thaw. Amazon stores ~150 Gt but switched to net source 2014-2019 from drought and deforestation.

mcqs.q: Why are tropical rainforest soils typically infertile?
options: Humans affect the carbon cycle by eating plants.
Heavy rainfall leaches nutrients, and most nutrients are stored in living biomass and rapidly recycled — the soil itself holds very little.
Because so much vegetation grows there, the soil must be fertile.
Because rainforest soils are made of clay.
